content_ta: Bybit CEO Ben Zhou, கிரிப்டோகரன்சி எக்ஸ்சேஞ்சுகள் ஹேக்கிங் அபாயங்களை தவிர்க்க முடியாதவை என்ற அடிப்படையிலேயே செயல்பட வேண்டும் என்று வலியுறுத்தியுள்ளார். வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் சொத்துக்களைப் பாதுகாக்கவும், நம்பிக்கையைப் பேணவும் நிறுவனங்கள் வலுவான பாதுகாப்பு நடவடிக்கைகளையும் அவசரகால திட்டங்களையும் முன்னுரிமை கொடுத்து செயல்படுத்த வேண்டும் என்று அவர் குறிப்பிட்டுள்ளார்.

content_ta: கிழக்கு கடற்கரை பகுதியிலுள்ள வாக்குப்பதிவு மையங்கள் மூடப்பட்டு வாக்கு எண்ணிக்கை தொடங்கப்பட்டுள்ள நிலையில், Kalshi கணிப்பு தளம் ஜனநாயகக் கட்சி மிகப்பெரிய வெற்றியைப் பெறும் என்றும் குடியரசுக் கட்சி பின்னடைவைச் சந்திக்கும் என்றும் கணித்துள்ளது. டிரம்ப் நிர்வாகத்தின் மீதான அதிருப்தி காரணமாக ஜனநாயகக் கட்சிக்கு ஆதரவான அலை வீசக்கூடும் என்ற எதிர்பார்ப்பு நிலவியது. நாடு முழுவதும் வாக்குகள் தொடர்ந்து எண்ணப்பட்டு வரும் நிலையில் முடிவுகள் வெளிவந்து கொண்டிருக்கின்றன.

title: South Korea’s ruling party formally proposes deferral of crypto income tax
summary: The party leader stated that the country should first enact the Digital Asset Basic Act, a comprehensive legal framework for crypto.
content: South Korea’s ruling party has formally proposed delaying the country's planned income tax on cryptocurrency. The party leader emphasized that South Korea should first establish the Digital Asset Basic Act, which will serve as a comprehensive legal framework for the crypto industry before implementing new taxes.
content_ta: South Korea-யின் ஆளும் கட்சி, cryptocurrency மீதான வருமான வரியை ஒத்திவைக்க அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாகப் பரிந்துரைத்துள்ளது. புதிய வரிகளை நடைமுறைப்படுத்துவதற்கு முன்பு, crypto துறைக்கான விரிவான சட்டக் கட்டமைப்பான Digital Asset Basic Act-ஐ South Korea முதலில் உருவாக்க வேண்டும் என்று கட்சியின் தலைவர் வலியுறுத்தினார்.

title: The Endgame of Cross-Border Payments Is an Operating System
summary:
PhotonPay argues that global B2B payments need a Financial OS combining fiat and stablecoin rails, FX and APIs to simplify cross-border money movement and make global commerce more accessible.
The post The Endgame of Cross-Border Payments Is an Operating System appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: PhotonPay highlights that the future of global B2B payments requires a comprehensive Financial OS. By combining traditional fiat rails, stablecoin rails, foreign exchange services, and APIs, this integrated operating system aims to simplify cross-border money movement and make international commerce significantly more accessible for businesses worldwide.
content_ta: PhotonPay நிறுவனத்தின் கருத்துப்படி, உலகளாவிய B2B பணப்பரிவர்த்தனைகளின் எதிர்காலத்திற்கு ஒரு ஒருங்கிணைந்த Financial OS அவசியமாகிறது. ஃபியட் மற்றும் stablecoin கட்டமைப்பு, அந்நிய செலாவணி சேவைகள் மற்றும் API-களை இணைப்பதன் மூலம், சர்வதேச வர்த்தகத்தை எளிதாக்க இந்த இயங்குதளம் உதவுகிறது.

title: North Korea denies Binance hack accusation, sees no need for US talks
summary:
The denial and diplomatic standoff highlight the complex interplay between cybercrime, international relations, and global security dynamics.

content: North Korea has officially denied accusations linking the country to the recent Binance hack. Alongside the denial, officials stated there is currently no need for diplomatic talks with the United States. This ongoing standoff highlights the complex challenges involving international cybercrime allegations and broader geopolitical relations between the nations.
content_ta: Binance ஹேக் சம்பவத்துடன் தொடர்புடைய குற்றச்சாட்டுகளை North Korea அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக மறுத்துள்ளது. இந்த மறுப்புடன், United States நாட்டுடன் இப்போதைக்கு பேச்சுவார்த்தை நடத்த வேண்டிய அவசியமில்லை என்றும் அதிகாரிகள் தெரிவித்தனர். சைபர் கிரைம் குற்றச்சாட்டுகள் மற்றும் நாடுகளுக்கு இடையேயான புவிசார் அரசியல் உறவுகளில் உள்ள சிக்கல்களை இந்த சம்பவம் வெளிக்காட்டுகிறது.

title: U.S.-sanctioned Moscow Exchange to list bitcoin and Tether’s USDT in December

title: Block Inc. shares rise 6% after-hours as it raises full-year profit forecast

title: Crediflow AI Secures £1.5M to Cut the Manual Work Behind Commercial Lending
summary:
A fintech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million to automate the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite.
Manchester-based Crediflow AI has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis.
The company uses AI to automate much of that work, which is typically spread across spreadsheets, PDFs, emails and other disconnected systems. Aggregating this data manually can sometimes take up to several days, but Crediflow says its platform reduces that time to between 10 and 30 minutes, giving credit teams more time to concentrate on critical tasks.
In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts, a process the industry calls financial spreading, analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format.
The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital.
The round was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), with investment also coming from Haatch and angel investors. The funding will accelerate development of the company’s platform, support engineering and product hires, and help Crediflow serve more banks and specialist lenders.
Crediflow will also extend automation across the loan lifecycle, with workflows tailored to each lender’s credit policies and processes. By bringing origination, underwriting and monitoring together, Crediflow aims to reduce repeated work and help lenders grow their loan books without an associated increase in administrative costs.
Last year, Crediflow became one of eight companies to receive funding from PXN’s PraeSeed programme, a 12-week cohort-based investment programme run in partnership with the British Business Bank and NPIF II to help scale early-stage businesses.
Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. Drey founded Crediflow after seeing first-hand how manual processes constrain lenders’ ability to grow.
Drey Kenfack, CEO and founder of Crediflow AI, said:
“Growing a loan book takes more than finding borrowers and having capital available. You need the capacity to assess those businesses, get decisions through approval and stay on top of risk once the money is out the door. I’ve spent much of my career doing that work.
“When every transaction requires hours of manual preparation, it affects how much business a lender can take on and which deals are worth pursuing. We built Crediflow to bring that workload down and give credit teams more time to understand the borrower and structure the financing.”
Joe Ball, senior investment associate at PXN Ventures, said:
“Businesses of all sizes and across all sectors often rely on commercial finance for a multitude of reasons, but the processes involved in granting this finance are often largely manual, making the process inefficient and slowing down lending decisions. By automating this area of the sector, Drey and the Crediflow AI team are not just supporting lenders but also removing barriers for companies that need funding to grow.”
Jonathan Keeling, partner at Haatch, said:
“The best B2B founders build the product they wished they’d had in their last job. Drey spent over a decade in credit roles watching good deals stall on admin, and Crediflow turns hours of manual spreading and memo writing into structured analysis credit teams can act on. With live customers across the UK, Europe and the US, the team has the traction to scale quickly, and we’re proud to support them on that journey.”
Sue Barnard, senior investment manager at British Business Bank, added:
“Through the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II, we’re backing the businesses that are helping to drive growth across the UK economy and improving productivity. With the opportunities from AI adoption holding the potential for further growth, innovative businesses like Crediflow AI are crucial to the UK remaining competitive internationally, while supporting the Government’s Industrial Strategy through digital and technology advancements.”
The £660m Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II) covers the entire North of England and provides loans from £25k to £2m and equity investment up to £5m to help a range of small and medium sized businesses to start up, scale up or stay ahead.
The purpose of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II is to drive sustainable economic growth by supporting innovation and creating local opportunity for new and growing businesses across the North of England. The Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II will increase the supply and diversity of early-stage finance for the North’s smaller businesses, providing funds to firms that might otherwise not receive investment and help to break down barriers in access to finance.

content_ta: Texas-ல் நடந்த தேர்தல் முடிவுகள் மற்றும் டெமாக்ரேட்டிக் கட்சியின் வெற்றி ஆகியவை டேட்டா சென்டர்கள் மீதான சாத்தியமான புதிய கட்டுப்பாடுகள் குறித்த கவலைகளை எழுப்பியுள்ளன. இந்த ஒழுங்குமுறை அழுத்தங்களுக்கு மத்தியில், Elon Musk மற்றும் Chamath Palihapitiya போன்ற தொழில்நுட்ப தலைவர்கள் விண்வெளிப் பொருளாதாரத்தின் மீது தங்கள் கவனத்தைத் திருப்பி வருகின்றனர். வேகமாக வளர்ந்து வரும் AI வர்த்தகத்தை ஆதரிக்க விண்வெளி அடிப்படையிலான டேட்டா சென்டர்களை அமைக்கும் புதுமையான சாத்தியக்கூறுகள் குறித்து அவர்கள் விவாதித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Morgan Stanley says it is among the first banks to tokenize real world assets
summary: The bank's announcement follows the launch of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation’s Tokenization Service, or DTS, on Oct. 28.
content: Morgan Stanley has announced that it is among the first traditional banks to tokenize real world assets. This development follows the official launch of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation’s Tokenization Service, known as DTS, which went live on October 28. The move highlights growing institutional interest in blockchain technology and asset tokenization within the banking sector.
content_ta: Morgan Stanley நிறுவனம் real world assets-ائ tokenize செய்யும் முதல் பாரம்பரிய வங்கிகளில் ஒன்றாக மாறியுள்ளதாக அறிவித்துள்ளது. Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation நிறுவனத்தின் Tokenization Service எனப்படும் DTS கடந்த அக்டோபர் 28 அன்று தொடங்கப்பட்டதை அடுத்து இந்த அறிவிப்பு வெளியாகியுள்ளது. இந்த நகர்வு வங்கித் துறையில் பிளாக்செயின் தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் மீதான ஆர்வத்தை காட்டுகிறது.

content: Justin Sun is seeking $264,000 in sanctions regarding World Liberty's UAE disclosure. Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in a California state court once the sanctions motion is resolved, with a hearing scheduled for December 10.

Sanctions தொடர்பான மனு மீது தீர்வு காணப்பட்டதும், California மாநில நீதிமன்றத்தில் தனது token-freeze வழக்கைத் திரும்பத் தாக்கல் செய்ய Sun திட்டமிட்டுள்ளார். இந்த வழக்கு விசாரணை வரும் டிசம்பர் 10-ம் தேதிக்கு ஒத்திவைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

content: A Polymarket trader has climbed to the top of the platform's leaderboard, securing a potential $917,000 payout following Democratic successes in the United States midterms. title: Judge Orders Bitcoin Wallet Returned to Family of Convicted Canadian Killer
summary:

content: A Canadian judge has ordered a Bitcoin wallet to be returned to the family of a convicted killer. title: BitGo launches institutional trading and financial solutions business led by former NYDIG executive
summary: BitGo has launched Global Markets, an institutional trading and financial solutions business headed by former NYDIG executive Pete Janney.
content: Cryptocurrency custodian BitGo has launched a new institutional trading and financial solutions business called Global Markets. The division will be led by former NYDIG executive Pete Janney. This expansion allows BitGo to offer enhanced financial services tailored specifically to institutional clients in the digital asset sector, further broadening its footprint in the cryptocurrency industry.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி கஸ்டடியன் நிறுவனமான BitGo, Global Markets என்ற பெயரில் புதிய நிறுவன வர்த்தக மற்றும் நிதி தீர்வு வணிகத்தைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. முன்னாள் NYDIG நிர்வாகியான Pete Janney இந்தப் பிரிவை வழிநடத்துவார். இந்த விரிவாக்கம், டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துத் துறையில் உள்ள நிறுவன வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்காகவே பிரத்யேகமாக வடிவமைக்கப்பட்ட மேம்பட்ட நிதி சேவைகளை வழங்க BitGo-வுக்கு உதவுகிறது.

content_ta: DeFi 201 என்பது ஒரு இணைக்கப்பட்ட புரோட்டோக்கால் அமைப்பாக decentralized finance-ஐ ஆராய்கிறது. title: 7 in 10 Brits Want Their Payments Handled by a UK or European Provider, With Data Privacy as the Main Reason
summary:
Seven in 10 (72%) UK shoppers say it matters to them that their payments are handled by a UK or European provider, according to new research from Brite Payments, the European Pay by Bank provider. The findings come as Brite Payments releases its report, Online Payments Report 2027: UK, which takes a deeper look at how UK consumers choose to pay online and who they trust with their financial data.
Shoppers’ preference for a UK or European provider is driven mainly by data protection, cited by 46% of those who want their personal financial data kept under UK and European privacy law. That’s ahead of protection from foreign political disputes or sanctions (22%), concern about foreign control of financial systems (17%) and keeping transaction fees in the UK and European economy (14%).
Shoppers are also changing how they pay. Four in 10 (40%) now often or regularly pay directly from their bank account when shopping online, almost exactly the same share as those who regularly pay by credit card (41%). 62% do so at least sometimes, and only 18% say they never have. Security is the main draw, with half (50%) citing it as a reason they would choose Pay by Bank, ahead of avoiding extra fees (37%).
Brite Payments’ founder and CEO, Lena Hackelöer, comments: “People choose how to pay based on convenience and trust. Shoppers want their financial data protected under UK and European privacy law, and they’re paying closer attention to where their money and data go when they click pay.
Paying directly from a bank account is now almost as common as using a credit card, and for merchants, that presents a tangible opportunity to offer a payment method that benefits both themselves and consumers in terms of privacy, convenience, and speed.  
Cards will always have a place at the checkout, but UK shoppers can now have a real choice in how they pay. The next step is making Pay by Bank as easy to find at checkout as it is to use.”

title: Conferma and VAT IT Partner to Streamline VAT Recovery on Hotel Spend
summary:
Conferma, the global leader in virtual card technology for business travel, today announced a partnership with VAT IT, experts in VAT recovery and tax compliance solutions, to make it simpler for businesses to recover VAT on hotel spend.
Once available, the integration will enable customers to transfer hotel invoice data collected through Conferma’s invoice collection service, Snap+, directly to VAT IT for reclaim processing. Now supported by Conferma’s direct API connectivity with hotel property management systems, Snap+ helps customers collect and process invoice data more efficiently. Connecting the services will create a more streamlined workflow from hotel payment and invoice capture through to VAT recovery.
VAT reclaim can be difficult to manage at scale, particularly for businesses operating across multiple jurisdictions. Eligibility rules, documentation standards, submission formats and deadlines vary by country, while recoverable VAT may be spread across high volumes of hotel invoices. Incomplete or inconsistent documentation can prevent otherwise eligible claims from succeeding, meaning VAT recovery may be missed, delayed or rejected. Global travel spend sits at over $1.7 trillion, with 44% of recoverable VAT never claimed.
For finance, tax and business travel teams, the challenge starts with obtaining the right invoice. The integration is designed to reduce that friction by securely passing hotel invoice data collected through Conferma directly into VAT IT’s reclaim process, supporting a more complete and consistent route from invoice capture to recovery.
The integration will help customers:
Reduce manual extraction, checking and submission of hotel invoice data
Create a more connected process from hotel payment to VAT recovery
Minimise errors associated with manual data handling
The companies will share further information about availability and customer access as the integration progresses.
Stuart Davenport, Chief Product Officer at Conferma, said: “Linking invoice capture directly with VAT IT’s recovery expertise will help customers reduce administration and improve the completeness of the data available for eligible VAT reclaims. It’s another step towards making business travel payments and the processes around them simpler and more connected.”
Scott Steenkamp, Partnerships Director at VAT IT, added: “Businesses can miss VAT recovery opportunities when invoice data is incomplete, fragmented or difficult to process. Connecting hotel invoice data collected through Conferma with VAT IT’s recovery expertise will give customers a simpler route to identify and recover eligible VAT across multiple jurisdictions.”

title: Mastercard Launches Free Cybersecurity Platform to Help Europe’s Small Businesses Build Cyber Confidence
summary:
Mastercard today announced the launch of Mastercard SME Academy: Cybersecurity, a free digital learning platform designed to help Europe’s small businesses build cyber confidence and take practical steps to protect themselves against common cyber threats.
The launch comes as Mastercard's Dreamonomics research highlights a significant gap between awareness and action when it comes to cybersecurity among Europe's small businesses.
While almost two thirds (64%) of SMEs in participating European markets say protecting their business from cyber threats is a high priority, only 37% are using cybersecurity tools such as antivirus software and firewalls.
Mastercard SME Academy: Cybersecurity
Small business owners often juggle multiple roles and responsibilities, leaving limited time to build expertise in areas such as cybersecurity.
Designed with those realities in mind, Mastercard SME Academy: Cybersecurity offers short, interactive learning modules that help small business owners better understand common cyber threats and take simple steps to strengthen their defences.  
Initially available in Ireland, Italy, Poland and the UK, the platform will be rolled out across Europe during 2027. It forms part of Mastercard’s commitment to provide free cybersecurity education to 10 million European SMEs by 2030.
The digital experience gives SMEs practical answers to common cybersecurity questions and is designed to help business owners take more informed action to protect their data, accounts, and devices. 
Learning covers how to recognise phishing and understand how data breaches happen; strengthen passwords and use multi-factor authentication; manage employee and third-party access; check links, downloads and attachments; protect business devices, recognise and respond to malware; reduce the risk of identity theft and impersonation; and secure critical business accounts.
Tulsi Narayan, Executive Vice President, Commercial and New Payment Flows Business, Europe at Mastercard says; “Every small business starts with a dream. Today’s small businesses are not short of ambition, but many do not have the time or resources to navigate an increasingly complex cyber landscape. Our Dreamonomics research highlights a clear gap between awareness and action. The Mastercard SME Academy: Cybersecurity platform is designed to help close that gap with practical, accessible learning that gives business owners the knowledge and confidence to protect against risk, so they can pursue their dreams with trust and confidence.”
Dreamonomics: Growth built on resilience and control
The findings from Mastercard's Dreamonomics research also highlight how SMEs across Europe are revisiting their approach to growth.
Across France, the Netherlands, Romania and the UK, nearly seven in ten (69%) SMEs prioritize predictability and stability over fast growth that involves taking risks and navigating uncertainty. Many (67%) also define success by building businesses that support their personal well-being.
Small business owners are also placing greater value on the customers they already have. More than six in ten (66%) would rather build deeper relationships with existing customers than maximise reach, pointing to the role of loyalty and trust in building sustainable growth.
As businesses adopt more digital tools and payment options, entrepreneurs are increasingly looking for solutions that are simpler and more connected. Seven in ten SMEs say integrated business tools are critical, while many are seeking greater visibility into financial performance and operations.
Across Europe, Mastercard provides the infrastructure to help propel small business growth, protect against risk and power their payments, so they can navigate the digital economy through insights, tools and initiatives designed to build resilience, strengthen digital confidence and support sustainable growth.
